questions.q: Per this lesson's testing checklist, what should you confirm about the deployer's TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE before calling the project finished?
options: That hasRole(TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, deployerAddress) actually returns false, not just assuming the renounce call worked
That the deployer's admin role was upgraded to a permanent role
That the admin role was transferred to the Governor contract
Admin role status does not need to be checked after deployment
questions.explain: The checklist explicitly calls for confirming the renounce actually took effect, rather than assuming it worked.

questions.q: Why doesn't a flash-loan-style attack work against this project's voting mechanism?
options: Voting power is checkpointed at a snapshot block, so tokens borrowed right before a vote had no recorded weight at that snapshot
Flash loans are technically impossible on any EVM-compatible network
The Governor contract rejects all transactions from smart contract wallets
Voting power is based on the number of days since a wallet was created
questions.explain: The lesson explains checkpointed (not live) balances are specifically what defeats this kind of attack.

questions.q: What happens to a timelock's protection if minDelay is set too low?
options: It stops providing real protection, leaving no meaningful window for the community to react to a bad proposal
The timelock automatically increases the delay on its own
Nothing changes -- minDelay has no effect on security
A low minDelay makes the quorum requirement irrelevant
questions.explain: The lesson states that a too-low minDelay removes the real protection the timelock is meant to provide.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend naming a real limitation in your own design during an interview, rather than claiming it has no weaknesses?
options: Honestly naming a limitation (like low-quorum capture) and what you'd change is a stronger answer than an implausible claim of perfection
Interviewers are legally required to reject any candidate who claims perfection
Naming a limitation guarantees a job offer
A design with no weaknesses is never possible to build at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames honest limitation-naming as a stronger interview answer than an unrealistic claim of a flawless design.

questions.q: What does the lesson say an interviewer is actually listening for when you present this capstone project?
options: Why you built it this way and what tradeoffs you made, not just a description of what it does
The exact number of git commits made during development
A word-for-word recitation of every line of Solidity code
Whether the frontend uses a specific color scheme
questions.explain: The lesson states an interviewer already assumes you can describe the system, and is really listening for your reasoning behind specific design choices.
